items.q: How is 4,300,000 written in scientific notation?

A forest stores <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.0 \times 10^{4}</annotation></semantics></math> kg of carbon on each of its <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.0 \times 10^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> hectares. How many kilograms of carbon does the whole forest store?

mistakes.why: You multiplied the exponents (4 × 3 = 12). When you multiply powers of ten, add the exponents: 4 + 3 = 7.
You divided 3.0 × 10^4 by 2.0 × 10^3. The total over all hectares is a product: kg per hectare × hectares.

items.q: A country has <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.4</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.4 \times 10^{8}</annotation></semantics></math> people and throws away <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>11</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.2 \times 10^{11}</annotation></semantics></math> kg of trash a year. How many kilograms of trash is that per person? (Divide the trash by the people.)

mistakes.why: You divided people by trash. Per person means trash ÷ people.
Check the front numbers: 1.2 ÷ 2.4 = 0.5, so the answer is 0.5 × 10^3 = 5 × 10^2, not 5 × 10^3.

items.q: A lake holds 750 ML (megaliters) of water. How many liters is that?
A water sample holds 2.5 g of dissolved salt. How many milligrams is that?

mistakes.why: You divided by 1,000. Milligrams are smaller units, so the number gets bigger: multiply by 1,000.

items.q: Four lakes hold these volumes of water. Which holds the most?

A landfill receives <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4.0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.0 \times 10^{5}</annotation></semantics></math> kg of trash a day. Write the setup for how much it receives in 30 days, with units, then give the answer.

mistakes.why: You divided by the days. A daily amount times the number of days gives the total.
The 30 days has no power of ten. Multiply 4.0 × 10^5 by 30 only.
4.0 × 30 = 120, so the answer is 120 × 10^5 = 1.2 × 10^7 kg. Moving the point one place adds 1 to the exponent.

items.q: Which city has the largest population?
options: North Falls and Lake City are tied

items.q: How many liters of water does Lake City use per person each year?

mistakes.why: You divided by 1.5 instead of 1.5 million. Write 1.5 million as 1.5 × 10^6 before you divide.

items.q: How many times more water does Lake City use in a year than North Falls?

mistakes.why: You divided North Falls by Lake City. "How many times more does Lake City use" puts Lake City on top.

items.q: Which city uses the most water per person?
options: The three cities use equal amounts per person

items.q: A town of 30,000 people uses 4,500,000 liters of water a day. How many liters is that per person per day?

mistakes.why: You divided people by liters. Per person means the total ÷ the number of people.
You multiplied. A per-person value divides the total by the population.

items.q: A family’s car used 1,200 liters of gasoline in 15,000 km of driving. Write the setup for the fuel used per km, with units, then give the answer.

mistakes.why: That gives km per liter. "Liters per km" puts liters on top: 1200 L / 15000 km.
That is km per liter (15000 / 1200). The question asks for liters per km.

items.q: Which value lets you compare how much water two cities of very different sizes use, fairly?
A lake’s water level drops 36 cm over 12 weeks of drought. What is the average rate of drop, in cm per week?

mistakes.why: You divided weeks by cm. A rate in cm per week puts cm on top.
You multiplied. A rate per week divides the change by the number of weeks.

items.q: A county of 2,500 square kilometers has 400,000 people. How many people live there per square kilometer?

mistakes.why: You divided area by people. Density is people ÷ area.

items.q: A school of 800 students throws away 2.4 metric tons of food each month. How many kilograms is that per student per month? (1 metric ton = 1,000 kg.)

mistakes.why: That is metric tons per student. The question asks for kilograms: change 2.4 metric tons to 2,400 kg first.

items.q: A leaky faucet drips 15 mL every minute. Which setup gives the liters lost in one day?
How many metric tons of trash per person did Alder collect in the year?

units: metric tons per person per year

mistakes.why: You divided people by trash. Per person is the trash ÷ the people.

items.q: Which town produced the most trash per person?
How many kilograms of trash per person did Birch collect? (1 metric ton = 1,000 kg.)

mistakes.why: 0.4 is in metric tons. Multiply by 1,000 to get kilograms.

items.q: A newspaper headline says "Birch is the most wasteful town." What does the per-person data show?
options: Birch has the largest total but the smallest per-person amount.
Birch is the most wasteful by both measures.
Birch has the most trash per person.
The towns are too different in size to compare.

items.q: A farm field covers 4.0 hectares. How many square meters is that? (1 ha = 10,000 m².)

mistakes.why: You divided by 10,000. Square meters are smaller than hectares, so the number gets bigger: multiply.

items.q: A water pump draws 2 kW and runs 6 hours a day for 30 days. Write the setup, with units, for the energy it uses, then give the answer in kWh.

mistakes.why: Energy is power times time, so multiply by 2 kW; dividing leaves units that do not make kWh.
That is in watt-hours (360,000 Wh). Multiply by 1 kW / 1,000 W, or use 2 kW, to get kWh.
That is in watt-hours (you used 2,000 W). Divide by 1,000 for kWh, or use 2 kW.
That is one day (6 h × 2 kW). The question asks for 30 days.

items.q: Electricity costs $0.15 per kWh. How much does 360 kWh cost?

mistakes.why: You divided 360 by 0.15. A price per kWh is multiplied by the kWh: 360 × 0.15.

items.q: A furnace burns natural gas that releases <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6.8</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.8 \times 10^{6}</annotation></semantics></math> BTU of heat in a winter. How many kWh is that? Use 1 kWh = 3,400 BTU (rounded).

mistakes.why: You multiplied by 3,400. To go from BTU to kWh, put BTU on the bottom of the factor: × 1 kWh / 3,400 BTU.

items.q: A car’s tank holds 25 gallons. Write the setup, with units, for the volume in liters, then give the answer. Use 1 gal = 3.79 L.

mistakes.why: Dividing leaves gal² per L. Multiply by 3.79 L per gal so the gallons cancel.
You divided 25 by 3.79. A liter is smaller than a gallon, so the number of liters is larger.

items.q: Which is a unit of power (a rate of energy use) rather than a unit of energy?
A 60-W light bulb is left on for 10 hours. How many kWh of energy does it use?

mistakes.why: 600 is in watt-hours. Divide by 1,000 for kilowatt-hours.
You divided by 100. A kilowatt is 1,000 watts.

items.q: A household uses 900 kWh of electricity a month. Its power company releases 0.4 kg of CO2 per kWh. How many kilograms of CO2 does the household’s electricity release in a year?

mistakes.why: That is one month. The question asks for a year: multiply by 12.
You divided by 0.4. Multiply the kWh by the kg of CO2 per kWh.

items.q: Write the setup, with units, for the energy the space heater uses in one day, in kWh. Then give the answer.

mistakes.why: That is in watt-hours (6,000 Wh). Multiply by 1 kW / 1,000 W to get kWh.
6,000 is in watt-hours. Divide by 1,000 for kWh.

items.q: Which appliance uses the most energy in a day?
At $0.15 per kWh, how much does it cost to run the refrigerator for 30 days?

mistakes.why: You left the energy in watt-hours. Divide by 1,000 to get kWh before multiplying by the price.
That is one day. Multiply by 30 days.

items.q: The family replaces the space heater with one rated 1,000 W, used the same 4 hours a day. How much energy does that save each day?
A town’s water use rose from 4,000 to 5,000 liters per day. Write the setup for the percent change, then give the answer.

mistakes.why: Divide by the old (starting) value, 4,000, not the new one.
Multiply by 100 to turn the fraction into a percent.
20% is the change divided by the new value. Divide by the old value, 4,000.
0.25 is the fraction. Multiply by 100: 25%.

items.q: A forest of 800 hectares lost 120 hectares to logging. By what percent did the forest area change?

mistakes.why: You divided by the new area (680). Percent change divides by the starting area, 800.
Multiply the fraction by 100 for a percent.

items.q: Coal provides 18% of a country’s 4.0 million GWh of electricity. How many GWh is that?

mistakes.why: You multiplied by 18, not 18%. Divide the percent by 100 first: 0.18 × 4,000,000.
You dropped "million". 18% of 4.0 million is 0.72 million = 720,000 GWh.

items.q: Of 2,500 kg of household waste, 650 kg was recycled. What percent was recycled?

mistakes.why: 0.26 is the fraction. Multiply by 100 for a percent.
You divided 2,500 by 650. The part (650) goes on top.

items.q: Which setup gives the percent change from 80 to 60?
Better insulation and new appliances cut a home’s electricity use from 9,600 kWh to 6,000 kWh a year. What is the percent decrease? Give a positive number.

mistakes.why: You divided by the new value (6,000). Use the starting value, 9,600.
3,600 kWh is the change itself. Divide by 9,600 and multiply by 100.

items.q: A fish population fell 50% one year and rose 50% the next. Compared with the start, the population is...
Write the setup for the percent change in frogs from 2020 to 2022, then give the answer.

mistakes.why: Put brackets around 150 - 120. Without them the division happens first.
Divide by the 2020 value (120), the starting value.
30 is the change in frogs. Divide by 120 and multiply by 100 for a percent.

items.q: What was the percent change in frogs from 2022 to 2024?

mistakes.why: You divided by 135. Percent change divides by the earlier value, 150 (and the change is a decrease).
The size is right, but frogs went down: the percent change is negative, -10%.

items.q: What was the percent change in frogs over the whole period, from 2020 to 2024?

mistakes.why: You added +25% and -10%. Percents of different starting values do not add; use the 2020 and 2024 counts.
You divided by 135. Divide by the 2020 count, 120.

items.q: Which statement describes the frog counts?
options: They rose 25%, then fell 10%, ending 12.5% above 2020.
They fell over the whole period.

items.q: A population grows 2% a year. Write the setup for its doubling time by the rule of 70, then give the answer.

mistakes.why: Use the growth rate as a percent (2), not as a decimal (0.02).
The rule of 70 puts 70 on top: 70 divided by the percent growth rate.
You divided by 0.02. Use the rate as a percent: 70 / 2.

items.q: A town of 50,000 people in 2024 grows 2.5% a year. In what year will it reach about 100,000 people?

mistakes.why: 28 years is the doubling time. The question asks for the year: add it to 2024.
You divided 70 by 0.025. Use the rate as a percent: 70 / 2.5 = 28 years, so 2024 + 28.

items.q: A lake’s algae population doubles every 14 days. What is its growth rate, in percent per day, by the rule of 70?

mistakes.why: You divided 14 by 70. Rate = 70 / doubling time.

items.q: A species has 400 individuals and a doubling time of 10 years. If the growth continues, how many will there be after 30 years?

mistakes.why: You multiplied by 3. Three doublings multiply by 2 three times: × 8.
That is 400 × 2 × 3. Each doubling multiplies by 2 again: 400 × 2 × 2 × 2.

items.q: Which change would cut a population’s doubling time in half?
A country’s population was 30 million in 2020 and grows 1.75% a year. In what year will it reach 60 million?

mistakes.why: 40 is the number of years. Add it to 2020 for the year.
You divided 70 by 17.5 instead of 1.75. Check the decimal point: 70 / 1.75 = 40.

items.q: A population of 6 million in 2020 grows 3.5% a year. About what will it be in 2060? Use the rule of 70, and keep the scale word in your answer (for example, 2.5 million).

mistakes.why: That is one doubling (to 2040). 2060 is two doublings: 6 × 2 × 2.
That is three doublings. 40 years at 20 years each is 2 doublings.
Keep the scale word: 24 million, not 24.

items.q: What is the doubling time of North Port?

mistakes.why: That is the year it doubles. The question asks for the doubling time in years.

items.q: In what year will Ridgeview reach about 2.4 million people?

mistakes.why: 50 years is the doubling time. Add it to 2025 for the year.

items.q: Which city will double its population soonest?
If Elm Falls keeps its growth rate, about how many people will it have in 2045?

mistakes.why: That is one doubling (to 2035). 2045 is two doublings away.
